newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end quiet session lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end quiet session lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended a very quiet session lower amid position-squaring before next week's heavy data line-up.
After rejecting the 106-31/32 session low early, June Treasury bond futures languished in a tight range in lower territory for the rest of the day.
"In the last hour and a half it was very quiet," said Don Pullen, trading floor bond manager for ED and F Man. "After hitting the low of the day, the market found some support."
Traders said next week's plethora of U.S. economic data was the next impetus for the market.
"Concerns still remain about the Fed raising rates at the May FOMC meeting, and some people expect the data to reinforce that," Pullen said.
March new home sales and durable goods are due Monday and Tuesday, respectively, with first-quarter employment cost index also due Tuesday. GDP and payrolls are due later in the week.
A bond futures trader said the overriding trend remained lower, but said next week's data would direct the near-term direction of the market.
"The data will reprice the market next week for the next big move," he said.
He said a week of strong data would push June T-bonds into the 104-00 handle by week's end.
"But it'll rally like crazy into the 109-00 handle if it's weak," he added. "We're probably poised to go two points either way."
A mixed bag of data would likely keep interest rate fears in the foreground, he said.
"There are three scenarios and two are negative."
The short end was extremely quiet on Friday, mostly following T-bonds, a Euro trader said. He pegged September Euro support at 93.66 and 93.62.

At the close, June T-bonds were off 6/32 to 107-3/32, 10-year notes fell 02/32 to 105-15/32, September T-bills were off 0.02 at 94.245, September Eurodollars were off 0.020 at 93.670 and December Eurodollars were 0.025 lower at 93.375.
